title: Nursery Third Term
overview: Third-Term Curriculum Intent Third Term completes the Nursery journey and provides a deliberate developmental bridge into Reception. First Term: BELONG -> COMMUNICATE -> NOTICE -> REPRESENT. Second Term: QUESTION -> INVESTIGATE -> COMPARE -> EXPLAIN -> SOLVE. Third Term: CONNECT -> APPLY -> CREATE -> REFLECT -> PREPARE. The term strengthens communication, self-regulation, physical development, phonological awareness, storytelling, meaningful mark-making, number sense, mathematical thinking, curiosity, problem-solving, creativity, Practical Life and independence without prematurely converting Nursery into Reception. The Nursery to Reception Bridge Nursery Development Third-Term Progression Communicate ideas Explain ideas increasingly clearly Listen to stories Retell, predict and create stories Hear rhyme and sounds Manipulate sounds increasingly Make meaningful marks Use marks/writing attempts for purposes Count objects Apply number understanding practically Notice quantities Compare and reason about quantities Notice pattern Continue and create patterns Explore shape Use shape and space in construction/problems Investigate Predict, test and explain Play collaboratively Plan and create with others Follow routines Manage routines increasingly independently Ask for help Attempt first and seek help appropriately Participate in self-care Take greater responsibility for self-care Explore ideas Represent and revisit ideas Transition principle: SECURE FOUNDATIONS BEFORE ACCELERATION Third-Term Curriculum Map Week Big Idea Main Development 1 Look How Things Grow Growth, change and sequencing 2 Life Cycles Around Us Change over time and observation 3 Our Amazing Earth Environment, land, water and stewardship 4 Nigeria - My Country Identity, place and belonging 5 Africa and the Wider World Widening geographical and cultural awareness 6 Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility Responsive review 7 Numbers Help Us Solve Problems Mathematical reasoning 8 Shapes, Measures and Patterns Spatial reasoning and comparison 9 I Am a Storyteller Narrative, language and imagination 10 I Can Plan, Make and Improve Design, creativity and problem-solving 11 Sounds, Words and Meaningful Marks Literacy foundations 12 I Can Do More for Myself Independence and Reception readiness 13 Moving Forward to Reception Reflection, celebration and transition Third-Term Communication Spine Adult interaction increasingly supports reasoning: 'Tell me more', 'What makes you think that?', 'What could happen next?', 'How are they the same/different?', 'What did you try?', 'Did it work?', 'What could you change?', 'Can you explain your idea?' Children's thinking is valued even before grammar is perfect. Nursery Year-End Phonological Awareness Children receive rich repeated opportunities to listen carefully, discriminate environmental/instrumental sounds, produce body percussion, join rhythm/rhyme, notice rhyming patterns, enjoy alliteration, experiment with voice sounds, hear words as sound sequences and experience oral blending/segmenting where appropriate. Some letter-sound knowledge may arise meaningfully, but Nursery remains a foundation for Reception systematic synthetic phonics. Nursery Year-End Literacy Entitlement Every child experiences daily stories, quality picture books, information books, rhymes, poetry/song, traditional tales, Nigerian stories, African stories, wider-world literature, storytelling, role play, drawing, mark-making, meaningful print, name recognition, fine-motor preparation and sound play. Progression: LISTEN -> TALK -> IMAGINE -> REPRESENT -> GIVE MEANING -> BEGIN TO WRITE. Nursery Year-End Mathematics Entitlement Children experience number, quantity, one-to-one correspondence, cardinality, subitising, comparison, small-number composition, more/fewer, pattern, shape, space, position, length, height, weight, capacity, sequence and practical problem-solving. Progression: EXPERIENCE -> NOTICE -> COMPARE -> REPRESENT -> REASON -> APPLY. Practical Life - End-of-Nursery Progression Crèche First Term: DO WITH ME -> Crèche Second: LET ME HELP -> Crèche Third: LET ME TRY -> Nursery First: I CAN DO MORE -> Nursery Second: I CAN TAKE RESPONSIBILITY -> Nursery Third: I AM BECOMING INDEPENDENT. Reception Readiness - The AMES Position Reception readiness is not primarily writing A-Z, reading long word lists, completing worksheets, counting artificially high or sitting silently for long periods. It includes communication, listening, conversation, books, sound play, meaningful marks, quantity understanding, practical problem-solving, confident movement, tool manipulation, personal needs, routines, participation, increasing emotional regulation, concentration, persistence, questioning, choice and appropriate help-seeking. READY DOES NOT MEAN FINISHED. Continuous Provision - Third Term Maintain books, mark-making, mathematics, construction, small world, role play, creative arts, Practical Life, investigation, sensory experiences, fine-motor resources and outdoor learning throughout the term. Do not remove play areas merely because Reception approaches. Outdoor Curriculum Include growth observation, gardening, nature, large construction, mathematical trails, routes, water/capacity, physical challenge, collaborative games, storytelling, large-scale art, sound investigation, shadow/light, problem-solving and environmental responsibility. Outdoor learning remains curriculum until the final Nursery day. Nigerian, African and Global Identity By year end children encounter: I am me; I belong to a family; I belong to Angel Montessori School; our school is in Owo; Owo is in Nigeria; Nigeria is a country in Africa; Africa contains many countries and peoples; there is a wider world. Progression: IDENTITY -> BELONGING -> PLACE -> COUNTRY -> CONTINENT -> WORLD. Christian Character - Year-End Spine Across Nursery children experience love, kindness, respect, gratitude, responsibility, service, patience, perseverance, gentleness, stewardship, wisdom, joy, fairness, cooperation, courage and hope. Character must be visible in adult modelling and relationships. Inclusion and SEND - Transition Transition identifies support needs and strengths across communication, home language, hearing, vision, sensory needs, physical/fine-motor development, social interaction, attention, self-regulation, toileting/self-care, medical needs, learning behaviours, interests, strengths and successful strategies. Transition information should answer: What does the next teacher need to know to help this child flourish from Day One? Parent Partnership - Reception Transition Encourage conversation, reading, rhymes, independence, dressing, toileting, handwashing, mealtime participation, tidying, simple responsibilities, meaningful counting, drawing, storytelling, physical activity, sleep routines and positive Reception discussion. Avoid unnecessary Reception 'entrance homework'. Nursery to Reception Transition Profile Summarise development across Communication & Language; PSED; Physical Development; Literacy; Mathematics; Understanding the World; Expressive Arts & Design; and Practical Life. Record how the child listens, communicates, cooperates, regulates, persists, moves, uses tools, manages self-care, engages with books/sounds/marks, understands number/shape/pattern, observes/investigates, creates and acts independently. Complete Nursery Annual Progression First Term - BELONG & REPRESENT: I BELONG -> I COMMUNICATE -> I NOTICE -> I REPRESENT. Second Term - INVESTIGATE & SOLVE: I QUESTION -> I INVESTIGATE -> I COMPARE -> I EXPLAIN -> I SOLVE. Third Term - CONNECT & PREPARE: I CONNECT -> I APPLY -> I CREATE -> I REFLECT -> I PREPARE. Full journey: BELONG -> COMMUNICATE -> INVESTIGATE -> REASON -> CREATE -> BECOME INDEPENDENT -> MOVE FORWARD. End-of-Nursery Curriculum Entitlement Every child leaving AMES Nursery should have experienced secure relationships, rich spoken language, daily books, songs/rhymes, phonological awareness, meaningful mark-making, number sense, mathematical reasoning, construction, investigation, nature, movement, outdoor learning, creative arts, music, storytelling, role play, Practical Life, self-care, community, Owo, Nigeria, Africa, the wider world, Christian character, problem-solving, choice, collaboration and increasing independence. NO CHILD'S NURSERY SUCCESS SHOULD BE JUDGED PRIMARILY BY THE NUMBER OF WORKSHEETS COMPLETED. Nursery Curriculum Quality Test Leadership asks whether children felt secure; adults knew them well; spoken language and books were rich; sound awareness and meaningful mathematics developed; children investigated, built, created and went outdoors; physical development and Practical Life increased independence; cooperation developed; Nigerian identity and Africa were represented authentically; Christian character was lived; SEND needs were supported; assessment improved teaching; parents were partners; and Reception transition was carefully planned. Central test: ARE OUR CHILDREN MORE COMMUNICATIVE, CURIOUS, CAPABLE AND INDEPENDENT THAN WHEN THEY ENTERED NURSERY? Nursery Year-End Declaration We helped children belong, listened to them, expanded language, surrounded them with books, sang and rhymed, developed sound awareness and meaningful marks, strengthened number sense, encouraged investigation and questions, built and created, solved problems, explored outdoors, cared for living things, strengthened friendships and self-regulation, gave real responsibilities, rooted learning in Owo and Nigeria, widened understanding towards Africa and the world, lived Christian character, recognised different developmental pathways, worked with families, allowed attempts and mistakes, and encouraged children to try again. We now prepare them to move forward because they are increasingly secure, communicative, curious, thoughtful, creative, responsible, capable, independent and ready for Reception. SECURE - COMMUNICATIVE - CURIOUS - THOUGHTFUL - CREATIVE - RESPONSIBLE - CAPABLE - INDEPENDENT - READY FOR RECEPTION HOW DOES THIS HELP THE CHILD FLOURISH? IN GOD WE TRUST. weeks.title: Look How Things Grow
weeks.curriculumIntent: Deepen understanding that living things change over time.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 1 - Look How Things Grow

items.title: Growth, change and sequencing
items.learningIntent: Deepen understanding that living things change over time.
items.learningContent:
Deepen understanding that living things change over time. Vocabulary: grow, change, seed, shoot, root, stem, leaf, flower, bigger,
taller, before, after. Observe and compare plants, notice change over days, use informal measurement, sequence, plant stories,
observation drawings and adult-scribed comments. Practical Life includes watering and care. Character: Patience and Stewardship.
items.teachingGuidance:
Observe and compare plants, notice change over days, use informal measurement, sequence, plant stories,
observation drawings and adult-scribed comments.
items.assessmentFocus:
Observe and compare plants, notice change over days, use informal measurement, sequence, plant stories,
observation drawings and adult-scribed comments.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 1 - Look How Things Grow

weeks.title: Life Cycles Around Us
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 2 - Life Cycles Around Us

items.title: Change over time and observation
items.learningContent:
Encounter patterns of growth and change through developmentally appropriate examples such as plant, butterfly, frog, chicken and
human growth. Vocabulary: baby, young, adult, egg, grow, change, first, next, later. Use photographs, books, models, sequencing,
retelling, movement, drawing, models and collage. The goal is conceptual encounter, not memorising scientific terminology.
Character: Wonder and Patience.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use photographs, books, models, sequencing,
retelling, movement, drawing, models and collage.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 2 - Life Cycles Around Us

weeks.title: Our Amazing Earth
weeks.curriculumIntent: Develop introductory understanding of the natural world and responsibility for it.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 3 - Our Amazing Earth

items.title: Environment, land, water and stewardship
items.learningIntent: Develop introductory understanding of the natural world and responsibility for it.
items.learningContent:
Develop introductory understanding of the natural world and responsibility for it. Vocabulary: Earth, land, water, river, sea, soil, tree,
sky, environment, clean, care. Explore land/water, soil, plants, weather, natural materials and environmental care without abstract
planetary science. Sort natural materials, compare, pattern and count; use nature stories and outdoor observation. Character:
Stewardship.
items.teachingGuidance: Sort natural materials, compare, pattern and count; use nature stories and outdoor observation.
items.outdoorLearning:
Explore land/water, soil, plants, weather, natural materials and environmental care without abstract
planetary science.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 3 - Our Amazing Earth

weeks.title: Nigeria: My Country
weeks.curriculumIntent: Strengthen identity through ME -> FAMILY -> SCHOOL -> OWO -> NIGERIA.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 4 - Nigeria: My Country

items.title: Identity, place and belonging
items.learningIntent: Strengthen identity through ME -> FAMILY -> SCHOOL -> OWO -> NIGERIA.
items.learningContent:
Strengthen identity through ME -> FAMILY -> SCHOOL -> OWO -> NIGERIA. Vocabulary: Nigeria, country, Owo, town, flag, green,
white, people, language, home. Encounter the flag, familiar places, foods, music, clothing, languages, landscapes, occupations,
transport and celebrations while communicating Nigeria's diversity. Use Nigerian stories, names, songs, environmental print and
open-ended creative work. Character: Gratitude, Respect and Belonging.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use Nigerian stories, names, songs, environmental print and
open-ended creative work.
items.nigerianAfricanContext: Strengthen identity through ME -> FAMILY -> SCHOOL -> OWO -> NIGERIA.
items.parentHomeConnection: Strengthen identity through ME -> FAMILY -> SCHOOL -> OWO -> NIGERIA.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 4 - Nigeria: My Country

weeks.title: Africa and the Wider World
weeks.curriculumIntent: Widen awareness through Owo -> Nigeria -> Africa -> Wider World.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 5 - Africa and the Wider World

items.title: Widening geographical and cultural awareness
items.learningIntent: Widen awareness through Owo -> Nigeria -> Africa -> Wider World.
items.learningContent:
Widen awareness through Owo -> Nigeria -> Africa -> Wider World. Africa is never taught as one country or culture. Children
encounter diversity in people, homes, cities, villages, landscapes, languages, music, food, clothing, animals and environments. Use
globes, maps, photographs and books exploratorily without map memorisation. Encourage respectful comparison and curiosity.
items.teachingGuidance: Africa is never taught as one country or culture.
items.nigerianAfricanContext: Widen awareness through Owo -> Nigeria -> Africa -> Wider World.
items.parentHomeConnection:
Children
encounter diversity in people, homes, cities, villages, landscapes, languages, music, food, clothing, animals and environments.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 5 - Africa and the Wider World

weeks.title: Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility
weeks.notes: Responsive review rather than formal examination.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility

items.title: Responsive review
items.learningContent:
No formal examination. Revisit growth, life cycles, nature, Nigeria, Africa, language, books, sound awareness, number, Practical Life,
movement, creativity and social development. Review progression and identify priorities for Reception transition.
items.outdoorLearning:
Revisit growth, life cycles, nature, Nigeria, Africa, language, books, sound awareness, number, Practical Life,
movement, creativity and social development.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.

Revisit growth, life cycles, nature, Nigeria, Africa, language, books, sound awareness, number, Practical Life,
movement, creativity and social development.
items.assessmentFocus:
Revisit growth, life cycles, nature, Nigeria, Africa, language, books, sound awareness, number, Practical Life,
movement, creativity and social development.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility

weeks.title: Numbers Help Us Solve Problems
weeks.curriculumIntent: comparison, one more/one fewer, small-number composition and subitising where secure.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 7 - Numbers Help Us Solve Problems

items.title: Mathematical reasoning
items.learningIntent: comparison, one more/one fewer, small-number composition and subitising where secure.
items.learningContent:
Apply number understanding to concrete practical problems involving sharing, combining/separating small groups, matching,
comparison, one more/one fewer, small-number composition and subitising where secure. Vocabulary: how many, more, fewer,
same, enough, another, altogether, left. Use counting stories, movement and distributing resources. Formal written arithmetic is not
the Nursery objective. Character: Perseverance and Fairness.
items.teachingGuidance: Use counting stories, movement and distributing resources.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 7 - Numbers Help Us Solve Problems

weeks.title: Shapes, Measures and Patterns
weeks.curriculumIntent: Apply mathematical thinking through construction, comparison and everyday problems.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 8 - Shapes, Measures and Patterns

items.title: Spatial reasoning and comparison
items.learningIntent: Apply mathematical thinking through construction, comparison and everyday problems.
items.learningContent:
Apply mathematical thinking through construction, comparison and everyday problems. Explore 2D shapes, 3D objects through play,
length, height, capacity, weight, position, pattern and sequence. Use longer/shorter, taller, heavier/lighter, full/empty, half-full
informally, behind, between and next to. Investigate containers, towers, patterns and fitting blocks. Character: Order and Persistence.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use longer/shorter, taller, heavier/lighter, full/empty, half-full
informally, behind, between and next to.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 8 - Shapes, Measures and Patterns

weeks.title: I Am a Storyteller
weeks.curriculumIntent: Organise experiences and imagination into narratives.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 9 - I Am a Storyteller

items.title: Narrative, language and imagination
items.learningIntent: Organise experiences and imagination into narratives.
items.learningContent:
Organise experiences and imagination into narratives. Develop character, setting, event, sequence, beginning, next and ending
naturally without testing terminology. Children retell, invent, change, dictate, act and discuss stories. Continue rhyme, rhythm,
alliteration, oral blending/segmenting where appropriate and sound discrimination. Include Nigerian/Yoruba oral storytelling traditions.
Character: Confidence and Creativity.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 9 - I Am a Storyteller

weeks.title: I Can Plan, Make and Improve
weeks.bigIdea: I Can Plan, Make and Improve
weeks.curriculumIntent: Undertake increasingly sustained projects using IDEA -> PLAN -> MAKE -> TEST -> CHANGE -> EXPLAIN.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 10 - I Can Plan, Make and Improve

items.title: Design, creativity and problem-solving
items.learningIntent: Undertake increasingly sustained projects using IDEA -> PLAN -> MAKE -> TEST -> CHANGE -> EXPLAIN.
items.learningContent:
Undertake increasingly sustained projects using IDEA -> PLAN -> MAKE -> TEST -> CHANGE -> EXPLAIN. Vocabulary: idea, plan,
make, join, test, change, improve, strong, problem, solution. Use open-ended construction, model-making, paint, textiles and loose
parts; investigate materials, shape, space, measure, pattern and balance. Draw plans, make labels and dictate explanations.
Products should not all look identical. Character: Creativity, Cooperation and Perseverance.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use open-ended construction, model-making, paint, textiles and loose
parts; investigate materials, shape, space, measure, pattern and balance.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 10 - I Can Plan, Make and Improve

weeks.title: Sounds, Words and Meaningful Marks
weeks.curriculumIntent: Consolidate literacy foundations without importing a Reception phonics programme.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 11 - Sounds, Words and Meaningful Marks

items.title: Literacy foundations
items.learningIntent: Consolidate literacy foundations without importing a Reception phonics programme.
items.learningContent:
Consolidate literacy foundations without importing a Reception phonics programme. Continue rhyme, alliteration, sound
discrimination, voice sounds, oral blending and oral segmenting where appropriate. Notice own/familiar names, labels, signs, books,
logos and meaningful environmental letters. Develop controlled mark-making, drawing, lines, curves, patterns, developmentally
appropriate name attempts and meaningful pretend writing. Fine motor: threading, pegging, dough, tongs, cutting and manipulation.
WRITING MUST GROW FROM COMMUNICATION AND MEANING.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 11 - Sounds, Words and Meaningful Marks

weeks.title: I Can Do More for Myself
weeks.bigIdea: I Can Do More for Myself
weeks.curriculumIntent: Prepare for Reception through independence, self-regulation and responsibility rather than accelerated worksheets.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 12 - I Can Do More for Myself

items.title: Independence and Reception readiness
items.learningIntent: Prepare for Reception through independence, self-regulation and responsibility rather than accelerated worksheets.
items.learningContent:
Prepare for Reception through independence, self-regulation and responsibility rather than accelerated worksheets. Children
increasingly manage belongings, hygiene/toilet routines with appropriate independence, eating/drinking, simple clothing/fastenings,
resources, spills and workspaces; wait, listen, follow routines, transition between activities, cooperate, manage disappointment with
support and attempt solutions. INDEPENDENCE IS ACADEMIC PREPARATION TOO. Character: Responsibility and Confidence.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 12 - I Can Do More for Myself

weeks.title: Moving Forward to Reception
weeks.curriculumIntent: Celebrate development and create a secure transition without pass/fail graduation testing.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 13 - Moving Forward to Reception

items.title: Reflection, celebration and transition
items.learningIntent: Celebrate development and create a secure transition without pass/fail graduation testing.
items.learningContent:
Celebrate development and create a secure transition without pass/fail graduation testing. Where practical, visit Reception, meet
adults, explore the room, see familiar resources, share a story, participate briefly and return to Nursery. Allow excitement and worry.
Create an 'Our Nursery Year' book using drawings, permitted photographs and dictated comments. Revisit mathematics and
celebrate through music, movement, art and story. Character: Courage, Gratitude and Hope.
items.teachingGuidance:
Where practical, visit Reception, meet
adults, explore the room, see familiar resources, share a story, participate briefly and return to Nursery.
items.assessmentFocus:
Revisit mathematics and
celebrate through music, movement, art and story.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Third Term / Week 13 - Moving Forward to Reception
